original.target_description: Experiment 1: reported matrices solved after recalling books versus Ten Commandments, in the recycle/opportunity-to-cheat conditions; planned contrast in the full four-cell ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Participants in the focal books/recycle versus Commandments/recycle comparison. Original paper prints 229 students for the entire four-cell experiment but does not print the two focal cell counts; the contrast-specific analytic n is not established here.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for Experiment 1; separate recycle-cell sample sizes are not printed in the original article.
n.location: p. 635 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1 Method; p. 636 (PDF p. 4), Results and Discussion
n.quote: Two hundred twenty-nine students participated in this experiment

es.location: p. 636 (PDF p. 4), Experiment 1 Results and Discussion, recycle-condition contrast

p.location: p. 636 (PDF p. 4), Experiment 1 Results and Discussion, recycle-condition contrast

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis of the Commandments-cheat minus books-cheat difference in self-reported matrices solved, 19 eligible laboratories. Fig. 2 is on printed p. 306 (PDF p. 8); primary-results prose is on printed p. 304 (PDF p. 6).

n.sample_role: Participants in the two mutually exclusive final cheat conditions contributing to the primary meta-analysis across 19 laboratories; 19 labs are the meta-analytic units.
n.exclusions: Excludes both control conditions. Source inclusion criteria: 18–25-year-old students, sample 20%–80% female, followed instructions and completed necessary tasks; exclusions for incorrect administration, sessions under 50, failure to tear out page, reporting over 20 matrices, or listing no books/Commandments and spending no recall time. Primary sample allows documented data-blind exceptions; 4,674 is the larger four-condition primary sample, not the target contrast N.
n.location: Printed p. 306, Fig. 2, Meta-Analytic Average row; p. 304, Inclusion criteria and Primary analyses.

es.metric: mean difference in matrices (Commandments-cheat minus books-cheat)
es.location: Printed p. 304 (article p. 6), Primary analyses; printed p. 306, Fig. 2.
es.quote: participants reported solving 0.11 more matrices in the ... Commandments-cheat condition than in the books- ... cheat condition (95% confidence interval, CI = [−0.09, ... 0.31]; Fig. 2).

reported_success.quote: In sum, we did not observe the predicted reduction ... in cheating following priming with the Ten Command- ... ments. These results call into question the effectiveness ... of using the Ten Commandments as a moral prime to ... reduce cheating.

notes:
The two supplied records have the same neutral description and page locators, with no distinct outcome/test identifier. Both therefore use the recycle-condition moral-reminder contrast, rather than the four-cell interaction or religiosity/heterogeneity tests. Original n is null: the printed total of 229 is for all four cells, and no focal two-cell analytic count is printed in that paper. The original article prints F and rounded cell means, but no mean-difference effect estimate: retained printed F even for requested mean difference, without subtracting rounded means. The replication prints a mean difference and Cohen’s d but no focal test statistic or p; retained mean difference even for requested test statistic. Its p = .78 belongs to heterogeneity and p = .20 to religiousness moderation, so neither was assigned to the focal effect. Replication n retains separately printed condition counts without summing them. The RRR also reports original-study values in Fig. 2; these were not substituted for the original paper’s printed test. Full-text titles verified against both supplied references.
Completion source review (n_r): Fig. 2 identifies final counts in the two mutually exclusive conditions of the primary contrast; control-condition participants are excluded. Participant N is distinct from the 19 laboratory meta-analytic units.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Primary moral-priming contrast reports mean difference 0.11 matrices, with CI [−0.09, 0.31]. Printed metric retained without conversion.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors explicitly state that they did not observe the predicted reduction in cheating; vocabulary failed records that narrative verdict.
